findings.evidence: MetricChange/Basic.lean:314-322 handles the case `h v v = 0`: `CFC.sqrt h♯ v = 0` follows from `inner_sqrt_apply_sqrt_apply hH`, and the unit is injective, so `v = 0`. That is the same statement as `inner_pos_left` for 𝕜 = ℝ.
findings.fix: Rewrite the forward direction of `isStrictlyPositive_continuousLinearMapOfBilin_iff` as `fun v hv ↦ by simpa [continuousLinearMapOfBilin_apply] using hT.inner_pos_left hv`. Consider proving `inner_pos_left` with the square-root argument (`inner_sqrt_apply_sqrt_apply` plus injectivity of the unit) instead of the 20-line quadratic expansion.
findings.issue: `IsStrictlyPositive.inner_pos_left` proves that a strictly positive operator is positive definite. The forward direction of the existing `isStrictlyPositive_continuousLinearMapOfBilin_iff` (MetricChange/Basic.lean:314-322) already proves the same fact over ℝ, with a shorter square-root argument. The repo now has two parallel proofs.

summary: The normalizing transport is new material, but the PR re-derives the same invertibility and pullback steps many times instead of factoring them into one lemma each, and proves strict positivity implies positive definiteness a second time beside an existing proof.
